title: The Certainty Trap
author: Greg McKeown
summary: Under pressure, speed mimics competence, and social reward for fast decisions teaches leaders to confuse decisiveness with clarity. Research on 'need for cognitive closure' shows time pressure drives people toward premature answers not because insight improved but because they want uncertainty to end. Making a decision reduces tension, and the reduction is mistaken for confidence. Resist premature closure by asking: is this clarity or just comfort?
points: Under pressure, speed looks like competence, and rewards for fast decisions teach confusion of decisiveness with clarity.
Cognitive closure research shows time pressure makes people settle early not because insight improves but because they want discomfort to end.
The relief of making a decision is not the same as being right.
Signalists resist premature closure by recognizing the urge to close the question to end discomfort.
Before making a fast decision, ask: is this clarity or just comfort, and can I invite one more view?
quotes: When we rush to decide, what often feels like clarity is usually just relief.
Under pressure, speed often looks like competence.
Participants who faced time pressure were more likely to settle on an answer quickly rather than keep searching.
The shift didn't happen because participants suddenly had better insight.
But relief is not the same as accuracy.” “Signalists don't avoid decisions, but they do resist making premature ones.” Archived from Substack on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
